title: Sorting: Bubble Sort
oneLiner: Repeatedly compare neighbors and swap if they're out of order -- the biggest unsorted value "bubbles" to the end each pass.
keyTakeaway: Bubble sort is O(n^2) -- up to n passes, each up to n comparisons -- and does almost nothing useful until the very end of each pass. It's simple to reason about, but the first sort to replace once performance on anything but a tiny or nearly-sorted input actually matters.
explanation: Walk the array comparing each adjacent pair; if they're out of order, swap them. One full pass like this guarantees the largest remaining value has "bubbled" all the way to the end -- so each pass can safely look at one fewer element than the last (the tail is already sorted). Repeat until a full pass makes zero swaps, which means the array is sorted. Watch out for the early-exit check: without it, bubble sort still works, it just wastes passes re-scanning an already-sorted array -- always O(n^2) instead of O(n) on the already-sorted best case.
